references.text: Later in the same conversation, the disciples ask Jesus to eat the food they have bought, which directly links back to their errand into the city to buy food ([ref:Joh 4:31-33|John 4:31-33]).
The disciples return from the city and are surprised that Jesus is speaking with the Samaritan woman – this concludes the errand described in verse 8 ([ref:Joh 4:27|John 4:27]).
Also at the feeding of the five thousand, there is a question about buying food for the crowd, where the disciples are confronted with the practical need for food ([ref:Joh 6:5-7|John 6:5-7]).
At the last meal, some of the disciples thought that Judas was sent out to buy what they needed for the feast – a similar errand where a disciple is sent to get supplies ([ref:Joh 13:29|John 13:29]).
Jesus tells the disciples that they themselves should give food to the crowd, which shows the disciples' role in providing food as a practical responsibility ([ref:Luk 9:13|Luke 9:13]).
